candidate.analysis: Analyze /input/public_csv by filtering ethics-focused debates, summarizing the target percentage increase by moderator stance and critical-event occurrence, computing correlations with numeric predictors, and fitting an ordinary least-squares model with stance indicators and the requested covariates. The program reports sample sizes, group means, correlations, and model coefficients while avoiding causal claims.
candidate.answer: Among 259 ethics-focused debates, utilitarian-moderated debates had a much higher mean percentage increase in utilitarian advocacy (65.189%) than deontological (0.054%) or virtue-ethics (0.570%) debates. Critical events were associated with higher mean increases (29.441% when true versus 6.143% when false; 18.046% for a blank/missing category). Audience interest, debate duration, and number of sessions showed negligible positive correlations with the outcome (-0.006, 0.074, and 0.053 respectively), while argument-intensity correlation was unavailable. The requested OLS model could not be estimated because of a singular design, so these are unadjusted associations and do not establish causation.
